title: Film Thickness Measurement - CD Variation Detection on Surfscan SP5
subtitle: Post-Planarization Quality Validation for 22nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Amir Patel

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Surfscan SP5 system to detect and classify CD Variation defects during post-planarization inspection at the 22nm technology node. The test is conducted at Dresden Fab 3 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for CD Variation defects that are critical to yield at the 22nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Surfscan SP5 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Surfscan SP5
- Inspection Type: Film Thickness Measurement
- Target Defect: CD Variation
- Process Step: Post-Planarization
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 22nm
- Fab Location: Dresden Fab 3

This test case applies to all Surfscan SP5 systems deployed at Dresden Fab 3 for post-planarization monitoring in the 22nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Surfscan SP5
Software Version: v11.6.134
Recipe: FILM_THICKNESS_MEASUREMENT_22nm_POST_PLANARIZATION
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Medium (192 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Surfscan SP5 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Film Thickness Measurement' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target CD Variation defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 22nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 108 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 96% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.2% for Film Thickness Measurement
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.98 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-06-26
Wafers Tested: 22
Total Defects Found: 2888
Defect Density: 919.28 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 6.5%
Capture Rate: 96.5%
Test Duration: 426 minutes
System Uptime: 99.7%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Surfscan SP5 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting CD Variation at the 22nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Edge-zone defect detection showed improved performance compared to previous revision.

e) The system successfully integrated with the factory automation host.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for CD Variation at 22nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
